source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economic Studies 91(6), 2024 final typeset version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: With no never-treated units, any nonzero nonnegative weighted sum over effects at event times at least the adoption-span threshold is not identified under its baseline untreated-outcome and no-anticipation assumptions.
The paper studies linear-function estimation in Gaussian indirect-data experiments, relates difficulty to a modulus of continuity, and gives near-minimax affine rules.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear functionals over convex regression classes under normal known-variance errors.
Theorem 3.1 verifies bias and variance regularity for boundary local-polynomial inference under a smoothness class and supports the paper's honest-CI calibration.

source_verification_receipts.version: author-hosted May 2020 article version corresponding to Journal of Econometrics 219 (2020)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Proposition 1 gives efficient influence functions and semiparametric efficiency bounds for ATT under panel and repeated-cross-section DiD settings.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a finite-dimensional algorithmic corollary specifying how to solve the modulus program and select the comparison depth, with complexity in T and a worked nonuniform-q instance.
Broaden the Gaussian-cell result to a triangular sub-Gaussian or clustered-cell approximation theorem, explicitly stating which covariance-estimation error leaves the exhaustion rate unchanged.
Add a boundary comparison against RambachanRoth2023 that formally separates smooth treatment-effect extrapolation from smooth violations of parallel trends on a shared design.

recommended_next_step: Advance this field-tier, two-axis-novel kernel to Stage 0; preserve the exact Gaussian scope and prioritize the bounded-lift proof.
